summary: All in src/finder. inline_rename.rs `add_and_rename`: reads the new entry's last-opened date when a view goes by it (`wants_last_opened`), opens the group the entry falls in (`open_group_of`, new in groups.rs: it decorates a copy of the entry as a row is decorated, asks `grouping::group_of`, and takes the label out of `collapsed_groups`; it does nothing in a view without groups), pushes the entry, makes the name field first (`begin_rename`) and the rows after it, selects the row (`select_only`, `select_row_in_columns`), scrolls to it now that it exists (`scroll_to_item`, split out of `begin_rename`), and calls the edit off (`cancel_rename`) when no row has the item. filter.rs `apply_filter_to`: the row at the path of a name being edited in the views (`renaming` with `!in_sidebar`) stays whatever `filter_keep` holds. inline_rename.rs `rename_ended` (new; called by `cancel_rename` and by `keyboard_back_from`, which `finish_rename` and `end_rename` go through): with a filter on and an edit made in the views it makes the rows again, in a `cx.defer`, so at the end of the effect cycle of the key or press that ended the edit (the review's fix: the implementer's commit made them again at once). mod.rs: `listed_len`, set in `rebuild_rows` after `apply_filter_to` and before `group_rows`; bars.rs `render_status_bar` counts it where it counted `rows.len()`. docs/manual.md: the status bar's two bullets, the Groups paragraph, the New Folder row, the filter paragraph.
changelog: New Folder left the keyboard in a name field that was never drawn when the list or icon view was in groups and the new folder's group was collapsed, or when a Nushell filter left the new folder out. After that the files took no key, and a click on an item selected nothing. The group now opens for the new folder, and under a filter the folder shows for as long as its name is being edited, then is filtered like any other item. An item being renamed also keeps its row when the filter answers again in the middle of the edit, where the edit used to end with half a name. The status bar now counts the items of collapsed groups too: it read "0 items" under headers that counted more, and "N of M items pass the filter" left out the items that pass in collapsed groups.
behaviour_changes: New Folder (Cmd+Shift+N, the Actions menu, the empty-space menu, the menu on an empty folder's message; the menu bar's File menu sends the same action) in a list or icon view in groups: when the new folder's group is collapsed it opens, the row or tile shows with the name field, the field has the keyboard, Return names the folder, Escape leaves "untitled folder", and the files have the keyboard afterward. Before, probed in review on the trunk's source: the header's count went up and no field was drawn; Down Arrow, letters and a click on a file's row did nothing; after a click on the status bar the files had the keyboard and still took no key; a click on the group's header showed a field that took no keys, and a name typed there with Return renamed nothing. Tested (the list by the key and by the message's menu, the icon view by the empty-space menu and the Actions menu), pictured (review-folder-collapsed-list, review-folder-collapsed-icons-dark), and probed in review in split view's second pane and in a file chooser.

The group that opened stays open afterward, also in the next folder the tab shows, as a group opened by a click does. The other groups stay as they were. In the column view and the gallery nothing is opened: the list's groups are as they were when the list is next chosen. Tested.

With the groups, the sort or a column by Date Last Opened, a new folder is listed under its date (Today) at once. Before, it showed under No Date until the folder was read again a moment later, and then moved. Tested.

With a Nushell filter on, New Folder shows the new folder's row (list, icons, the first column of the column view) with its name field, before the filter has answered for it and after, until the edit ends by Return, Escape, a click elsewhere or any other way. Then it is held to the filter like any other item: it leaves the list unless the filter's latest answer has it, and in the column view its own column closes with it. In the gallery the Rename dialog opens as before, and the folder is listed only if it passes. Before: no row, no field, and no key did anything. Tested, pictured (review-filter-list-dark, review-filter-named-list), and probed in review from a search with a filter on and the folder's group collapsed as well: the search ends, the group opens, the row shows with its field.

F2 under a filter: the row of the item being renamed stays when the filter answers again in the middle of the edit and leaves the item out. Before, the row went, the item got what had been typed so far, and the keys that followed went to the files. Tested.

When an edit in the views ends with a filter on, the rows are made again right after the key or press that ended it. A press on another item that ends the edit selects the item pressed: tested in the list, in a folder and among a filtered search's results, and probed in the icon view and the first column. Among a filtered search's results that is what the trunk did before this change; the implementer's commit had the press select the item after the one pressed (review_fixes, the first).

Status bar: "N items", the M of "N of M selected" and the N of "N of M items pass the filter" count the items of collapsed groups. The items of a folder open in place in the list count as they did, and go on counting when their group is collapsed. Before: "7 items" under headers that counted 16, "0 items" with every group collapsed. Tested, pictured (review-all-collapsed-status-list: "15 items" under five collapsed headers that add up to 15).
While a new folder is named under a filter the bar reads "1 of N selected", N counting the folder that shows in spite of the filter (pictured: "1 of 4 selected" with three files passing).

Manual: the status bar's two bullets (how many items are listed, collapsed groups counted), the Groups paragraph (the bar goes on counting; New Folder opens its group, which stays open), the New Folder row, and the filter paragraph (an item whose name is being edited in place stays listed until the edit ends).
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.
No general net for a name field that is never drawn: only New Folder's path is covered. One state stays as it was (Found, not fixed, the first): a folder that can't be listed but can be written to.

The fallback in `add_and_rename` (`None => self.cancel_rename(..)`) has no test. It is reached only when the new folder can't be read back right after it was made, which no test can arrange; the implementer's mutation that removes it fails nothing.

An edit that ends while the filter's run for the new folder is still out, as with Escape or a click right after New Folder: the row is held to the answer that was made before the folder existed, so it goes, and comes back unselected when the run answers if the folder passes. In the column view the folder's own empty column then stays open with nothing selected in the first column (probed on the implementer's commit: [[notes.txt], []]; the review's fix doesn't change it). It is the wart column-pane-selection-by-path's record describes for renames under a filter, and it is filter-stale-keep-set's ground. See the note for that brief.

After naming under a filter, a folder whose new name passes is listed again only when the filter has answered for the renamed row, and is not selected. The same happens after any rename under a filter on the trunk before this change.
New File… does not open a collapsed group for the new file: the file lands in its collapsed group, unselected, with the header's count up by one. The keys work (guard test).
A new folder whose given name puts it in another, collapsed group (grouped by Name with A collapsed, named "Archive") goes into that group once named, unselected, as any renamed item does.

No kept test sends the events of a double-click one at a time. The harness sends a click's move, press and release in one update, so what is made at the end of the press's effect cycle comes after the release there. Probed in review with each event in an update of its own, as the app gets them.

Nothing was compiled or run for macOS or Windows. No cfg-gated code is touched, no existing signature changed, and src/term, src/macos.rs, src/win.rs and examples call nothing that changed (grep). `cargo clippy --features term` was not run.
README.md and the Search Syntax dialog state nothing this changes.
Not tested separately: the menu bar's File > New Folder (the same action).

review_fixes: Found with a probe and fixed: with a filter on, a press on another item that ended an edit acted on the item after it. The implementer's `rename_ended` made the rows again at once. A press outside the name field ends the edit in the capture phase of that press (`on_mouse_down_out`), and the row the press lands on handles it in the bubble phase by its index among the rows as they were drawn (`press_on_row(ix, ..)`, `click_row(ix, ..)`, `right_click_row(ix, ..)`, `press_on_column_row(col, ix, ..)`). So when the edited row left the list at that moment and was above the row pressed, the press selected the next item. Probed on the implementer's commit: a new folder that doesn't pass the filter, named, then a click on the row under it (zeta.txt) selected zulu.txt; the same with the name left untouched; with the events sent one at a time as the app gets them, a double-click on zeta.txt opened zulu.txt (the recorded call was Open(zulu.txt)). It was also a regression for something the trunk did right: F2 on an item among a filtered search's results, as in a Smart Folder with a filter, then a click on the next row to end the edit, selected the row after it (the renamed row waits there for the filter's answer under its new name); on the trunk's source the same steps select the row clicked. Fix: `rename_ended` makes the rows again in a `cx.defer`, at the end of the effect cycle of the event that ended the edit, when every listener of that press has run; the selection is then carried over by path. Test: a_click_that_ends_a_name_under_a_filter_selects_the_item_clicked, seen failing on the implementer's commit (zulu note.txt selected where zeta note.txt was clicked) and with the rebuild taken out altogether.

On the trunk's source: what the window did after New Folder with the folder's group collapsed (behaviour_changes, the first), and F2 among a filtered search's results ended by a click (the clicked row was selected). On the implementer's commit and again on the fix: a click on the row under a new folder being named under a filter, with a name typed and with none; the same press and release, and a double-click, sent one event to an update; a right-click there; the same click in the icon view and in the first column; Escape pressed before the filter had answered, in the columns and in the list. The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code and the probes say. (1) A press or a key that acts on another item than the one aimed at, because the rows move under it. That was real: review_fixes, the first. With the fix the rows change only at the end of the effect cycle of the event that ended the edit, so every listener of that event sees the rows as they were drawn: the row's own handler, a right-click's selection, a box started in empty space, and the menu the kit builds in a deferred callback of its own (it is queued after the rebuild and reads a selection that was carried over by path). What is left is that the rows under the pointer move up by one when the named row goes. The second click of a double-click then lands on the next item and selects it; nothing is opened, since c0605b6 opens only when both clicks are on the same item (probed). A right-click selects the item pressed and its menu is not drawn, because the row is no longer under the pointer; the files have the keyboard, and Down Arrow goes on from the item pressed (probed). Without a filter the rows move the same way, by reading, whenever a renamed item sorts elsewhere. (2) The keyboard left in a field that nothing draws, which is what this fixes. I went through every way a folder is made and every view. By its key, the Actions menu, the empty-space menu and the message's menu (tests), from a search with a filter on and the group collapsed, in split view's second pane and in a file chooser (probes), the row is there, the field has the keyboard, and the files have it afterward. The gallery and New File… ask in a dialog. The tree's New Folder names its folder in the tree (test). A second New Folder during the first's naming takes the field over. The fallback for a folder that got no row is reached only when the folder can't be read back right after it was made. One state is not covered and was not before: a folder that can't be listed but can be written to (Found, not fixed). (3) The list or the bar saying something untrue: a row the filter leaves out that stays after its edit, or a count that is off. Only `renaming` exempts a row; every way an edit ends goes through `rename_ended`, except leaving the place (`location_changed`), which reads the rows again, and an edit that another one replaces: a second New Folder, whose own rebuild follows at once, or, by reading, the tree's Rename… chosen after a name was refused in the views, where the row stays until the rows are next made. `listed_len` is set in `rebuild_rows`, the only place that assigns `rows` (grep), right after the filter and before the groups, so it can't fall out of step with them.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) The group that opens for a new folder stays open, in this folder and in the next one the tab shows. Collapsing it again would hide the folder just named; the manual says what happens. (b) A folder named under a filter it doesn't pass leaves the list when Return is pressed, with no word that it was made: the filter bar and the status bar's "N of M items pass the filter" are what say why. The brief's other design was to start no edit and say that the filter hides the folder. (c) "15 items" with every group collapsed counts what no row shows. The manual now says the bar counts the items of collapsed groups. (d) One more file read on the window's thread for a new folder when a view goes by Date Last Opened, beside the two that were there. (e) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows.

For briefs still to come.
- filter-stale-keep-set: between New Folder and the filter's answer the list holds what the last answer kept plus the new folder's row, with `is_filtering()` true; after the answer the same, until the edit ends. The exemption is one more term in `apply_filter_to`'s `retain` (`|| named == Some(path)`, `named` being the path of `renaming` when it isn't in the sidebar): keep it whatever becomes of the keep-set. At the end of an edit `rename_ended` (inline_rename.rs) queues one `rebuild_rows` with `cx.defer`, only with a filter on and not for a tree rename; the row is then held to `filter_keep` as it is at that moment. If the run that was started for the rows with the new folder is still out then (Escape or a click within the run's time), that keep-set was made without the folder: the row goes and comes back unselected when the run answers, if the folder passes, and in the column view `sync_root_column`'s `!self.filtering` guard leaves the folder's own empty column open ([[notes.txt], []] in a probe). I tried skipping the queued rebuild while `self.filtering` (the run's end rebuilds anyway). It cures the case when no other rebuild comes in between, but the quiet reload that follows New Folder rebuilds too, and in a test the order of that reload and the run's answer goes by the seed, so it could not be pinned and I took it out. If your change stops holding rows to an answer that was made without them (the new path is not among the paths the keep-set answered for), both go away, and the queued rebuild is still needed for a folder the answer leaves out. Tests that state what the list holds while a run is out: a_new_folder_is_named_in_its_row_whatever_the_filter_keeps (the last answer's rows plus the folder), and a_click_that_ends_a_name_under_a_filter_selects_the_item_clicked, whose `assert_eq!(ui.names(), found[1..])` says a renamed result's row is gone right after the click; if you keep such a row listed until its run answers, that one line changes and the selection lines stay.
- fix-rename-press-selection: with a filter on, the end of an edit now also makes the rows again, queued with `cx.defer` in `rename_ended` (called from `cancel_rename` and `keyboard_back_from`), so after the press's own listeners and before the reload that `submit_rename` asks for can end. Without a filter `rename_ended` only notifies, so your scenario's steps are as the brief has them. a_click_that_ends_a_name_under_a_filter_selects_the_item_clicked holds before and after your fix: in its first half the renamed folder never passes, so the reload finds nothing to select; in its second half (F2 among a filtered search's results) it reads the selection only right after the click, because after settling, by reading, the reload selects the renamed item when the filter has answered for its new name before the reload ends, which is your fault, and the order of the two goes by the seed there. With your fix `assert_eq!(ui.selected(), [found[1].as_str()])` can follow its last `settle()`. A right-click that ends an edit while the edited row is above the row pressed and leaves the list (a filter on) selects the row pressed and draws no menu, the row having moved from under the pointer: the case of your second reviewer's first precision.
- fix-filter-reruns-and-fresh-rows: `apply_filter_to`'s `retain` has the exemption's term, and `rebuild_rows` sets `self.listed_len = rows.len()` right after `apply_filter_to` returns; keep both when `filter_source` comes to hold sizes and dates. `rename_ended` asks for one more `rebuild_rows` at the end of an edit under a filter; with the source unchanged it starts no run. A new folder is pushed onto `listing` with the dates read at that moment and no size, and the reload that follows reads the same.
- stale-rows-on-place-change (lane f): the status bar reads `listed_len`, set in `rebuild_rows` beside `unfiltered_len`. If you empty `rows` anywhere else, reset both, or go through `rebuild_rows`, or the bar goes on counting the place left. `add_and_rename` pushes the new entry onto `self.listing` and makes the rows at once, also while a place is still being read (`loading`), when the listing is that of the place left and the folder was made in the new one; if rows are dropped or inert while a place is read, New Folder pressed then needs a look. `location_changed` still drops `renaming` without `rename_ended`, which is right as long as the rows are read again there.
- select-all-perf: `rebuild_rows` has one more line between `self.apply_filter_to(&mut rows, cx)` and the name styles, `self.listed_len = rows.len()`. It has to stay after the filter and before `group_rows`. The status bar's `count` is `self.listed_len` now, where collapsed-groups-empty-view's record says `rows.len()`.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: `open_group_of(&FileEntry)` (groups.rs) opens the group an item falls in, for a view that shows groups, and is called only for a new folder. a_new_folder_in_a_view_without_groups_leaves_them_collapsed makes a folder in the column view, where it is selected, then chooses the list and expects the Folder group still collapsed and the folder not listed. If a selection kept through the switch should open its group, that test's last line changes with it.
- icon-tile-hit-target: a_new_folder_from_a_menu_opens_its_collapsed_group_in_the_icon_view right-clicks `content` 300 points in and 20 above its bottom edge, under the tiles, and expects the empty-space menu with New Folder.
- context-menus-fit: tests click the item labelled New Folder in the empty-space menu, the Actions menu, the message's menu and the tree's menu.
- split-active-pane: New Folder by its key goes to the pane that has the keyboard, and its field is in that pane (probed with the second pane grouped and its Folder group collapsed).
- files-changed-off-thread: `add_and_rename` reads the one new entry on the window's thread (`FileEntry::from_path`, and `read_last_opened` when `wants_last_opened()`). If that moves off the thread, the field still has to be made before the rows are (the exemption reads `renaming` at the rebuild), and the row has to exist in the same update, or the edit is called off.
- idle-redraw-after-search, search-start-no-flash, type-select-space: `rename_ended` asks for one rebuild of the rows for each edit that ends under a filter, and none otherwise.
- column-row-menu-wrong-item, inactive-selection-colour, collapsible-sidebar-sections, go-to-folder-keyboard, tab-drop-and-close, restore-session-tabs, quick-look-empty-state, preview-page-keys, thumbnail-memory, accented-names-search, near-miss-beside-scattered: independent. `render_column_row`, the sidebar and the previews are not touched.

Found, not fixed (there before, outside this brief).
- By reading only, since root is never refused here: in a folder that can't be listed but can be written to (a drop box, mode -wx), the file area shows "Can't open this folder" in the views' place, New Folder still makes the folder, and `add_and_rename` finds a row for it (the entry is pushed onto the emptied listing) that no view draws. The keyboard is then in a field that is never drawn, as in this brief, until the window goes elsewhere. `add_and_rename` could call the edit off when `listing_error` is set, or `new_folder` could leave the naming out there.
- New Folder's key works while a name is being edited, and what was typed for the first item is dropped without a word: `start_rename_field` replaces `renaming`, and nothing ends the edit it replaces (probed: "First" typed, Cmd+Shift+N, and the first folder is still "untitled folder").
- New Folder and a rename don't tell the window's other tabs and pane (`tell_others` is called only from `files_changed`), so another pane on the same folder shows the new folder, or the new name, at its next two-second look (seen in the split view probe).
- The second click of a double-click that ends an edit lands on whatever has moved under the pointer by then, and selects it (probed under a filter, above; by reading the same without one, when the renamed item sorts elsewhere).
